saints.name: St. Anthony Zaccaria
saints.title: Priest and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A physician turned priest who founded the Barnabites and preached reform of morals in Milan…
biography: Born at Cremona in December 1502, Anthony Mary Zaccaria studied philosophy at Pavia and medicine at Padua, then practiced as a physician in his native city for three years. Finding his call in the cure of souls, he was ordained in 1529 and in 1530 followed the Countess Ludovica Torelli to Milan.

There, with Bartolomeo Ferrari and Giacomo Antonio Morigia, he gathered companions in the Oratory of Eternal Wisdom, preaching in churches and on street corners. In 1533 the community began its common life, sanctioned that year by Clement VII as the Clerics Regular of St. Paul — called Barnabites after the Milanese church of St. Barnabas.

He promoted frequent Communion, devotion to the Passion — reviving the ringing of Milan's bells at three o'clock on Fridays — and in 1534 popularized the Forty Hours' exposition of the Blessed Sacrament. Twice investigated for heresy and twice acquitted, he died at Cremona on 5 July 1539, aged thirty-six, and was canonized in 1897 by Leo XIII. Physicians claim him as patron for the medicine he once practiced.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Barnabites and reviving fervent devotion to the Eucharist.
